chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so I said, 'The performer of Tamattu' covers his head when he shaves [it].' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son! Shaving his head is greater [in significance/act] than covering it.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: The pilgrim who performs Hajj al-Tamattu'

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on covering the head versus shaving it for the Mu'tamatti' during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for the Mu'tamatti', the shaving of the head (halq) is the definitive act that terminates the state of Ihram, rendering the subsequent covering of the head a secondary matter. This highlights the jurisprudential principle that the completion of the major ritual act supersedes minor preparatory or concluding actions, emphasizing the transformative nature of halq in concluding the Hajj rites.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws, so I said, ‘The performer of Tumatto covers his head after he shaves off (his head)’. So heasws said: ‘O myasws son! Shaving off of his head is greater than covering it up’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is for al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous); if he can cover his head after shaving. He (the Imam) said, ‘Son, shaving is greater than his covering it.’”
